title: Ithaca: deep neural network for restoring, placing and dating ancient Greek inscriptions (capability study)
summary: Ithaca restores and dates Greek inscriptions with measured accuracy gains; no specific accepted restoration verified (general benefit without an event).
account: On 9 March 2022 Nature published Ithaca, a deep neural network built by DeepMind with the Universities of Venice Ca' Foscari, Oxford and Athens (Assael, Sommerschield, Prag, de Freitas and others) to restore missing text in damaged ancient Greek inscriptions and to attribute them to a place and date. Ithaca restored text with 62 percent accuracy on its own and raised historians' accuracy from 25 to 72 percent when they worked with it; it attributed inscriptions geographically with 71 percent accuracy and dated them to within about 30 years. Its average date of 421 BC for a group of disputed Athenian decrees agreed with recent independent re-dating. The fetched sources report accuracy studies and a public interface, not a specific inscription whose restoration epigraphers have since accepted.
purpose: Built to restore, geographically attribute and date ancient Greek inscriptions; the reported capability was that purpose.
system: Ithaca (transformer-based deep neural network for epigraphic restoration and attribution)
developer: DeepMind with Ca' Foscari University of Venice, University of Oxford and Athens University of Economics and Business
deployer: Research consortium; public interface at ithaca.deepmind.com

ratings.reason: General benefit without an event: the fetched sources give accuracy measurements and a prediction that agrees with independent re-dating of Athenian decrees, but no discrete, verified downstream result attributable to Ithaca.

ai_role.statement: Ithaca's outputs were evaluated against held-out ground truth and in a study of historians working with and without it; the 421 BC dating is a model prediction consistent with evidence established by other means, not an outcome the model caused.

Verification sweep: both sources were written by Ithaca's developers (DeepMind and Ca' Foscari), so the Ca' Foscari page is now marked vendor-authored and a Nature News & Views by Charlotte Roueché, who is not an author of the paper, is added as the independent source.
